chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Adam, from his father through his chain, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

O Ali! Do not consult with a coward, for he will narrow your exit; and do not consult with a miser, for he will restrain you from your goal; and do not consult with a greedy person, for he will make his evil appear attractive to you. And know, O Ali, that cowardice, miserliness, and greed are a single nature, united by bad opinion (of God).
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of people one should avoid consulting according to this hadith, and what is their common root?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, the Prophet (peace be upon him) warns Ali (peace be upon him) against consulting the coward, the miser, and the greedy, explaining that these three distinct vices share a common root: *su' al-zann* (bad opinion of God). This theological insight highlights how a deficient view of divine providence manifests practically as fear of loss (cowardice), hoarding (miserliness), and insatiable desire (greed). The narration underscores the Shia emphasis on aligning one’s external actions with internal spiritual states when seeking counsel.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-57 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Adam, on the authority of his father through a chain of documentations that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “O Ali! Do not consult with a coward since he would hinder your progress. Do not consult with a miser since he would lower your aspirations; and do not consult with a greedy person since he would guide you towards collecting wealth. O Ali! Know that cowardliness, miserliness and greed are of the same nature. They all stem from having a bad opinion about God.”
